literal: Taizong, Part One
idiomatic: Taizong, Part One

literal: The Taizong, Emperor of Filial Martial Bounty and Cultured Letters — taboo name Deguang, courtesy name Dejin, childhood name Yaogu.
idiomatic: Taizong, styled the Filial Martial Bounty and Cultured Letters Emperor, bore the taboo name Deguang, courtesy name Dejin, and childhood name Yaogu.

literal: The Taizu's second son; his mother was Empress Chunqin, née Xiao.
idiomatic: He was the Taizu's second son, born to Empress Chunqin of the Xiao clan.

literal: Born in the second year of Tang Tianfu, divine light was unusual; hunters captured a white deer and a white hawk, and people took them as auspicious signs.
idiomatic: He was born in the second year of the Tang Tianfu era (902). Unusual divine light attended his birth, and hunters took a white deer and a white hawk—signs the people read as heaven's favor.

literal: When grown, his appearance was stern and dignified yet his nature generous and humane; he decided many affairs of army and state.
idiomatic: Grown to manhood, he looked grave and imposing yet was by nature generous and humane, and on many matters of army and state his word prevailed.

literal: In the first year of Tianzan, he was appointed Grand Marshal of All Armies and Horses Under Heaven, and soon received orders to command the Six Armies southward to conquer territory.
idiomatic: In the first year of Tianzan he was made Grand Marshal of All Armies and Horses Under Heaven, and soon after was ordered to lead the Six Armies south in conquest.

literal: The next year he took Pingzhou and captured Zhao Siwen and Zhang Chong.
idiomatic: The next year he seized Pingzhou, taking Zhao Siwen and Zhang Chong prisoner.

literal: On the return he broke the Xi chief Husun at Arrow Mountain, and all the tribes submitted.
idiomatic: On the homeward march he routed the Xi chieftain Husun at Arrow Mountain, and every tribe submitted.

literal: Again he led troops to raid Zhen and Ding; wherever he went, they fortified and dared not give battle.
idiomatic: He marched again against Zhen and Ding; everywhere his host appeared, the enemy barricaded themselves and would not fight.

literal: The army halted at Youzhou; Fu Cunshen resisted south of the prefecture, sent troops to intercept, was greatly defeated, and Deputy Generals Pei Xin and several dozen men were captured.
idiomatic: When the army camped at Youzhou, Fu Cunshen made a stand south of the city and sent troops to intercept; he was routed, and Deputy General Pei Xin and dozens of others were taken.

literal: Moreover, following the Taizu he broke the Yujueli tribes, settled the Tangut along the Yellow River banks, took the commanderies of Shanxi, seized the Uyghur Chanyu City, pacified Bohai to the east, and broke the Dalugu — ten thousand li east and west, wherever he went there was achievement.
idiomatic: Following the Taizu he crushed the Yujueli tribes, subjugated the Tangut along the riverbanks, overran the garrisons of Shanxi, took the Uyghur Chanyu City, subdued Bohai in the east, and broke the Dalugu — over ten thousand li in every direction he won distinction.

literal: First and Second Years of Tianxian
idiomatic: First and Second Years of Tianxian

literal: In the seventh month of the first year of Tianxian, the Taizu died, and the Empress assumed charge of military and state affairs.
idiomatic: In the seventh month of Tianxian's first year the Taizu died, and the Empress Dowager assumed regency over army and state.

literal: The next autumn, work on the ancestral tombs was completed.
idiomatic: The following autumn the ancestral tombs were finished.

literal: In the eleventh month of winter, on renxu day, the Human Sovereign King Bei led the ministers to petition the Empress, saying: "The Crown Prince and Grand Marshal's merit and repute — within and without all look to him; he should inherit the great succession.
idiomatic: That winter, in the eleventh month on renxu day, the Human Sovereign King Bei led the court in petition to the Empress: "The Prince, Grand Marshal — the realm looks to his merit and prestige; he should take up the Great Succession.

literal: " The Empress agreed.
idiomatic: The Empress assented.

literal: That same day he ascended the imperial throne.
idiomatic: That day he ascended the throne.

literal: On guihai day he visited the Taizu temple.
idiomatic: On guihai day he paid homage at the Taizu's temple.

literal: On bingyin day he performed the firewood-pledge rite.
idiomatic: On bingyin day he performed the ceremonial investiture rite.

literal: On wuchen day he returned to the capital.
idiomatic: On wuchen day he returned to the capital.

literal: On renshen day he presided in the Xuanzheng Hall; the ministers offered the honorific title Emperor Who Succeeds the Sage.
idiomatic: On renshen day he took his seat in the Hall of Promulgating Governance; the ministers presented the elevated title Emperor Who Succeeds the Sage.

literal: A general amnesty was declared.
idiomatic: A general amnesty was proclaimed.

literal: The relevant offices requested a change of era name; it was not granted.
idiomatic: Officials petitioned to change the era name; he refused.

literal: In the twelfth month on gengchen day, the Empress Dowager was honored as Grand Empress Dowager, the Empress as Yingtian Grand Empress Dowager, and Consort Xiao was installed as Empress.
idiomatic: In the twelfth month, on gengchen day, he raised the Empress Dowager to Grand Empress Dowager and the reigning Empress to Yingtian Grand Empress Dowager, and crowned Consort Xiao as Empress.

literal: When the rites were complete, he inspected the attendants' roster and arrangements.
idiomatic: After the ceremonies he reviewed the roster of personal attendants.

literal: On xinsi day the generals of all circuits took leave and returned to their posts.
idiomatic: On xinsi day the military governors of every circuit took leave and returned to their commands.

literal: On jichou day he sacrificed to Heaven and Earth.
idiomatic: On jichou day he offered sacrifice to Heaven and Earth.

literal: On gengyin day he dispatched envoys to notify the various states.
idiomatic: On gengyin day he sent envoys to announce his accession to the tributary states.

literal: On xinmao day he inspected the herds in the near suburbs.
idiomatic: On xinmao day he reviewed the imperial herds in the outskirts of the capital.

literal: On wuxu day the Jurchen sent envoys with tribute.
idiomatic: On wuxu day Jurchen envoys arrived bearing tribute.

literal: On renyin day he visited the Taizu temple.
idiomatic: On renyin day he again paid homage at the Taizu's temple.

literal: On jiachen day he inspected the officials of the Banners and Drums, Guest Reception, and other offices.
idiomatic: On jiachen day he reviewed the personnel of the banner, drum, and guest-reception bureaus.

literal: On dingwei day an edict ordered the selection of Yaolian clan descendants from the nine tents fit to hold office.
idiomatic: On dingwei day an edict called for suitable sons of the nine Yaolian tents to be chosen for office.

literal: Third Year of Tianxian
idiomatic: Third Year of Tianxian

literal: In the third year, on jiyou day in the first month of spring, he inspected the northern troop registers.
idiomatic: In his third year, on jiyou day in the first month of spring, he reviewed the northern military rolls.

literal: On gengxu day he inspected the southern troop registers.
idiomatic: On gengxu day he reviewed the southern military rolls.

literal: On dingsi day he inspected the three armies: Pishi, Zhuaila, and Moli.
idiomatic: On dingsi day he inspected the Pishi, Zhuaila, and Moli armies.

literal: On jiwei day the Jurchen of Luonie River in Huanglong Prefecture and the Dalugu sent tribute.
idiomatic: On jiwei day Jurchen from Luonie River in Huanglong Prefecture and the Dalugu presented tribute.

literal: On gengwu day Wang Yu was made Military Governor of the Xingguo Army and continued as Palace Secretary.
idiomatic: On gengwu day Wang Yu was appointed Military Governor of the Xingguo Army while retaining his post as Palace Secretary.

literal: In the second month, he proceeded to Changbo.
idiomatic: In the second month he traveled to Changbo.

literal: On jihai day Chief Minister Nieli Gun presented a white wolf.
idiomatic: On jihai day Nieli Gun, Chief Minister, presented a white wolf.

literal: On xinchou day the Dalugu sent tribute.
idiomatic: On xinchou day the Dalugu sent tribute.

literal: In the third month, on yimao day, he hunted to the east.
idiomatic: In the third month, on yimao day, he rode east on the hunt.

literal: On guihai day he hunted at Mountain of Wild Boars.
idiomatic: On guihai day he hunted at Wild Boar Mountain.

literal: On yichou day he hunted at Pine Mountain.
idiomatic: On yichou day he hunted at Pine Mountain.

literal: Wang Du, Military Governor of Tang's Yiwu Army, sent men bringing Dingzhou to submit.
idiomatic: Wang Du, Tang's governor of the Yiwu Army, dispatched envoys offering Dingzhou in surrender.

literal: The Tang ruler sent troops to attack him; envoys came begging relief, and orders were issued for Tieci of the Xi Tulii tribe to go rescue him.
idiomatic: The Tang emperor marched against him; Wang Du sent envoys pleading for aid, and the court ordered Tieci of the Xi Tulii to his relief.

literal: In the fourth month, on wuyin day, he toured east.
idiomatic: In the fourth month, on wuyin day, he made an eastern progress.

literal: On jimao day he sacrificed to the Elk Spirit.
idiomatic: On jimao day he offered sacrifice to the Elk Spirit.

literal: On dinghai day at the hunt grounds, private and public persons were permitted to take feather, hide, and wood materials.
idiomatic: On dinghai day at the hunting grounds he permitted all to gather feathers, hides, and wood.

literal: On jiawu day arrow wood was taken at Red Mountain.
idiomatic: On jiawu day they cut arrowwood on Red Mountain.

literal: On bingshen day he hunted at Three Mountains.
idiomatic: On bingshen day he hunted at Three Mountains.

literal: Tieci defeated Tang general Wang Yanqiu at Dingzhou.
idiomatic: Tieci routed Tang general Wang Yanqiu at Dingzhou.

literal: Tang forces massed in strength; Tieci requested reinforcements.
idiomatic: Tang armies massed; Tieci asked for more troops.

literal: On xinchou day Chief Minister Nieli Gun and Commander Chala were ordered to go aid him.
idiomatic: On xinchou day Nieli Gun and Commander Chala were dispatched to reinforce him.

literal: In the fifth month, on bingwu day, the Heavenly Feast Hall was built.
idiomatic: In the fifth month, on bingwu day, the Heavenly Feast Hall was erected.

literal: He hunted at Suola Mountain.
idiomatic: He hunted at Suola Mountain.

literal: On wushen day he returned from the hunt.
idiomatic: On wushen day he returned from the hunt.

literal: On dingmao day Tolun, Master of the Hunt, was ordered to campaign against the Wugu tribe.
idiomatic: On dingmao day Tolun was sent to subdue the Wugu.

literal: On jisi day the Jurchen sent tribute.
idiomatic: On jisi day the Jurchen presented tribute.

literal: In the sixth month, on jimao day, the Seser rite was performed.
idiomatic: In the sixth month, on jimao day, he performed the Seser rite.

literal: In the seventh month of autumn, on dingwei day, Tolun presented the triumph over the Wugu.
idiomatic: In the seventh month of autumn, on dingwei day, Tolun presented his victory over the Wugu.

literal: On renzi day Wang Du reported that Tang troops had broken Dingzhou; Tieci died in the fight, and Nieli Gun, Chala, and several dozen others were taken prisoner.
idiomatic: On renzi day Wang Du reported that Tang forces had stormed Dingzhou: Tieci had fallen, and Nieli Gun, Chala, and dozens of others were captured.

literal: The Emperor, because the campaign had been ill-timed, deeply regretted it and lavishly rewarded the families of officers and men killed in battle.
idiomatic: The Emperor, judging the campaign mistimed, bitterly regretted it and heaped gifts upon the families of the fallen.

literal: On gengwu day he performed rites at the Taizu temple.
idiomatic: On gengwu day he offered sacrifice at the Taizu's temple.

literal: In the eighth month, on bingzi day, the Turks sent tribute.
idiomatic: In the eighth month, on bingzi day, the Turks sent tribute.

literal: On gengchen day an edict ordered the erection of a birth-stele for Yingtian Grand Empress Dowager at Yikun Prefecture.
idiomatic: On gengchen day an edict ordered a monument to the birth of Yingtian Grand Empress Dowager erected at Yikun Prefecture.

literal: In the ninth month, on jimao day, Tolun dispatched men presenting Wugu captives.
idiomatic: In the ninth month, on jimao day, Tolun sent captives from the Wugu campaign.

literal: On guiwei day an edict ordered distribution of gifts among the ministers.
idiomatic: On guiwei day an edict distributed gifts among the ministers.

literal: On jichou day he visited the residence of the Human Sovereign King Bei.
idiomatic: On jichou day he called upon the Human Sovereign King Bei.

literal: On gengyin day envoys were sent to Tang.
idiomatic: On gengyin day he dispatched envoys to Tang.

literal: On xinmao day he again visited the Human Sovereign King.
idiomatic: On xinmao day he again called upon the Human Sovereign King.

literal: On guisi day the relevant offices requested that the Emperor's birthday be made the Heavenly Bestowal Festival and the Empress Dowager's birthday the Everlasting Peace Festival.
idiomatic: On guisi day officials petitioned that the Emperor's birthday be observed as the Heavenly Bestowal Festival and the Empress Dowager's as the Everlasting Peace Festival.

literal: In the tenth month of winter, on the guimao new moon, on the Everlasting Peace Festival the Emperor led the ministers to offer longevity felicitations at Yanhe Palace.
idiomatic: That winter, on the guimao new moon of the tenth month, at the Everlasting Peace Festival the Emperor led the court in offering birthday felicitations at Yanhe Palace.

literal: On jiyou day he visited the Taizu temple.
idiomatic: On jiyou day he paid homage at the Taizu's temple.

literal: Tang sent envoys presenting a jade flute.
idiomatic: Tang sent envoys bearing a jade flute as a gift.

literal: On jiazi day, the Heavenly Bestowal Festival, the Emperor presided in the Hall of Five Phoenixes receiving felicitations from ministers and envoys of various states.
idiomatic: On jiazi day, the Heavenly Bestowal Festival, the Emperor took his seat in the Hall of Five Phoenixes to receive felicitations from the court and foreign envoys.

literal: In the eleventh month, on bingzi day, the Biegude sent tribute.
idiomatic: In the eleventh month, on bingzi day, the Biegude sent tribute.

literal: On xinchou day he personally led a campaign against Tang.
idiomatic: On xinchou day he took the field in person against Tang.

literal: In the twelfth month, on guimao day, he sacrificed to Heaven and Earth.
idiomatic: In the twelfth month, on guimao day, he sacrificed to Heaven and Earth.

literal: On gengxu day, learning that the Tang ruler had again sent envoys on a diplomatic mission, the Emperor asked his attendants; all said: "Tang has repeatedly sent envoys; they truly fear our might.
idiomatic: On gengxu day, hearing that Tang had once more sent envoys, the Emperor asked his counselors. All replied: "Tang keeps sending envoys — they fear our power.

literal: One should not lightly undertake action; it is best to watch for an opening and then move.
idiomatic: We should not strike rashly; let us watch for an opening and move when it comes.

literal: " The Emperor agreed.
idiomatic: The Emperor approved.

literal: On jiayin day he halted at Xingguo; Tang envoys arrived, and he then withdrew the army.
idiomatic: On jiayin day he encamped at Apricot Ravine; when Tang envoys arrived, he turned the army homeward.

literal: At that time the Human Sovereign King was at the imperial capital; an edict ordered Yelü Yuzhi to relocate Eastern Dan households to fill Dongping.
idiomatic: The Human Sovereign King was then at the capital; an edict charged Yelü Yuzhi with resettling Eastern Dan households to populate Dongping.

literal: Some of those people fled into Silla and Jurchen lands; therefore an edict was issued that those too impoverished to move might be supported and placed under wealthy households of the upper realm.
idiomatic: Some fled into Silla or Jurchen territory; an edict then permitted impoverished families unable to move to be supplied and placed under the care of wealthy households of the realm.

literal: Dongping Commandery was elevated to Southern Capital.
idiomatic: Dongping Commandery was raised to Southern Capital.

literal: Fourth Year of Tianxian
idiomatic: Fourth Year of Tianxian

literal: In the fourth year, on the renshen new moon in the first month of spring, he feasted ministers and envoys of various states and watched acrobats and wrestling performances.
idiomatic: In the fourth year, at the renshen new moon of the first spring month, he held a banquet for the court and foreign envoys and watched acrobats wrestle.

literal: On jimao day he went to Guaguo.
idiomatic: On jimao day he proceeded to Melon Ravine.

literal: In the second month, on gengxu day, he inspected the Yaolian clan household registers.
idiomatic: In the second month, on gengxu day, he reviewed the household registers of the Yaolian line.

literal: In the third month, on jiawu day, he performed distant sacrifice to the multitude of spirits.
idiomatic: In the third month, on jiawu day, he offered distant sacrifice to the host of spirits.

literal: In the fourth month of summer, on xinhai day, he returned from Guaguo.
idiomatic: In the fourth month of summer, on xinhai day, he returned from Melon Ravine.

literal: On renzi day he visited the Taizu temple.
idiomatic: On renzi day he paid homage at the Taizu's temple.

literal: On guichou day he visited the Taizu's traveling palace.
idiomatic: On guichou day he paid homage at the Taizu's traveling palace.

literal: On jiayin day he went to Tiancheng Army and visited the ancestral tombs.
idiomatic: On jiayin day he traveled to Tiancheng Army and paid homage at the ancestral tombs.

literal: On xinyou day the Human Sovereign King Bei came to court.
idiomatic: On xinyou day the Human Sovereign King Bei came to court.

literal: On guihai day he reviewed prisoners.
idiomatic: On guihai day he reviewed the prisons.

literal: In the fifth month, on guiyou day, he visited the Hall of the Two Principles and feasted the ministers.
idiomatic: In the fifth month, on guiyou day, he visited the Hall of the Two Principles and feasted the court.

literal: The Jurchen sent tribute.
idiomatic: The Jurchen sent tribute.
